trust.reason: Container wiring and decorators; resolution failures are programmer errors at boot.
Logging must never be the reason a call site needs a try/catch.

Assigns the status code field and returns res (dinner dist chunk createCompatPair); no validation, cannot throw. setHeader/redirect/cookie/clearCookie stay distrusted: they valueOrThrow on invalid headers/cookies.
Stores the body and sets flags; serialization happens later in dinner's pipeline, which maps failures to a Result. Cannot throw at the call site.
See @noego/dinner.CompatResponse.json.
Sets the ended flag and returns res; cannot throw.
Method decorator applied at class definition; binds the method to its SQL. The query's own failures surface when the method is called, not at the decorator. Same entry as desktops/demo-assistant.
Class decorator naming the database for every @Query method; applied at class definition. See sqlstack.Query.

Sets the open transaction's rollbackOnly flag and rollbackError on the handle's own state (sqlstack 3.6.0 dist/esm/transactions.js:48); no I/O, cannot throw. Same role as sqlstack.rollback in desktops/demo-assistant.
Reads the AsyncLocalStorage store size (sqlstack 3.6.0 dist/esm/transactions.js:243); never resolves a database or connects, cannot throw.

Map lookup in the AsyncLocalStorage store plus a TransactionHandle construction (sqlstack 3.6.0 dist/esm/transactions.js:247); cannot throw. SqlStack.getEntry, which can throw on a closed stack or a missing default, stays distrusted.
Returns the process-wide resolver slot (sqlstack 3.6.0 dist/esm/core/resolver.js:84); cannot throw.
Throws only for an invalid header name; every call site passes a literal name.

Every call site passes a literal status (or one copied from an existing Response) and a body we hold. Status 101 + webSocket sites run only in Cloudflare Workers/Durable Objects, which accept it. Static Response.json stays distrusted (serializes).
Returns a UUID string; defines no failure in Workers or Node.
Synchronous form throws only for an invalid size; every call site passes a literal (16/18/32).
Throws only for an unknown algorithm; every call site passes the literal "sha256".
Throws only for a wrong argument type or after digest(), both programmer errors TypeScript or call order prevent.
Throws only when called twice on the same Hash, a programmer error.
Pure length computation; throws only for a wrong argument type, which TypeScript prevents.
Throws only for a non-integer or negative delay; call sites pass numeric constants.
Returns a timestamp.
Sets a flag on the event; cannot fail.
Serializes an already-parsed URL; cannot fail. The URL constructor stays distrusted.
Returns an iterator over parsed params; cannot fail.
